evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 東字甲骨部件分析
evidence.text: Database analysis says oracle-bone and bronze forms depict a sack containing material, tied at both ends, and gives “bag” as the original graphic sense. It says 東 was used by borrowing for the direction east in both oracle-bone and bronze material, citing the oracle-bone inscription 合集9735「東土受年」 and the poem 詩·召南·小星「三五在東」. It relates 東, 橐, 㯱, and 束 graphically and says 東 and 束 differentiated from one character. This is the database's analysis, not direct proof of the pictured item's spoken name.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析（東）

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 說文 comparison in 形義源流通解
evidence.text: The database quotes the Eastern Han 說文解字 entry:「東，動也。从木。官溥說：从日在木中。」It rejects the analysis of 東 as sun within a tree as an explanation of the graph. This is a historical account preserved by 說文, not confirmation of the early graphic origin.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析（東）

evidence.source: 陳雅雯, 成大中文學報 27, article “說「東」”
evidence.field: discussion of competing paleographic and loan analyses, pp. 158–160
evidence.text: The author disputes treating every early 東-shaped graph as a sack: she notes that many oracle-bone occurrences appear in personal, palace, place, and ritual names rather than an attested sack sense, and argues that assigning the original sense 橐囊 remains debatable. She also objects that a sound-only loan from 橐 to 東 is insufficiently demonstrated without explaining the graphic image's role; she treats the Shuowen and Dong-Fusang cultural reading as a possible substantive tradition and cites Allan's analysis of forms containing elements interpreted as 日 and 木. Thus the bag account is a well-supported database analysis but not an uncontested conclusion.
evidence.title: 說「東」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The cited oracle-bone example 合集9735「東土受年」 uses 東 for the eastern region; the database also cites Western Zhou bronze inscriptions 臣卿鼎「公違省自東，才（在）新邑」 and 殷簋「東啚（鄙）五邑」 for east/eastern territory. These establish directional use in early inscriptional contexts independently from the proposed original bag referent.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析（東）

evidence.text: The received poem contains「嘒彼小星，三五在東」, a dated literary attestation of 東 with directional meaning. The online page supplies the poem text but does not establish when this particular wording was first written down; no exact composition or manuscript date is established here.
evidence.title: 詩經: 國風: 召南: 小星

evidence.field: 東西南北, part 1, sections 東 and 束/橐
evidence.text: The article proposes bag-like origins for 東, 束, and 橐, reports 東 and 束 used interchangeably in bronze inscriptions, and analyzes east as a sound loan. It compares Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms 東 *tˤoŋ and 束 *s-tʰok, describing shared initial/root material despite differing codas. It also explains simplified 东 as derived from a cursive shorthand of 東. This is a modern specialist account; the specific name and pronunciation of the pictured sack are not independently recovered, so the phonetic pathway from the object's name to the word for east remains a proposal.
evidence.title: Explaining the Directions 東西南北, part 1: 東西

evidence.source: Outlier Linguistics, citing Baxter and Sagart
evidence.text: Outlier gives a simplified Baxter–Sagart 1.1 Old Chinese comparison: 東 *tˤoŋ and 束 *s-tʰok; it gives 橐 *tʰˤak and 石 *dAk for a separate sound-component discussion. These are reconstructions, not recorded pronunciations. The piece discusses 橐 and 石 as an internal phonetic relation, distinct from the claim that the whole graph 東 was borrowed to write “east.” No object-name pronunciation for the pictured bag is provided.
evidence.title: Explaining the Directions 東西南北, part 1: 東西

evidence.field: pronunciation, historical readings, definitions and character sources
evidence.text: The page records modern Standard Mandarin dōng (Pinyin) and Cantonese dung1, Middle Chinese fanqie 德紅切 with Baxter transcription tuwng, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *tˤoŋ (including a noted possible *tˤoŋʔ), and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *toːŋ. It lists east, host/owner, and other later senses, and presents the Shuowen entry. These separate reconstruction systems should not be collapsed into one form.
evidence.title: 東 dōng - 汉典

evidence.text: Their University of Michigan project page identifies the supplementary reconstruction lists as materials for Baxter and Sagart's 2014 Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction. The specific entry-level 東 reconstruction was inspected on the Han Dian page, not verified in the project site's downloadable list during this search.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

evidence.text: The dictionary records east/direction and cites Shuowen's「動也」and the Eastern Han period text 白虎通·五行「東方者，動方也，萬物始動生也」as an explanatory association. It records host/landlord senses under the rationale that the host sat on the east side, with a Tang Du Fu example「東家蹇驢許借我」. This supports a traditional cultural semantic explanation for host/owner, but does not supply the first attestation of that extension. The dictionary also lists spring and toilet senses without establishing their chronology or semantic paths; these are not treated here as securely connected stages.
evidence.title: 東 dōng - 汉典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The source analyzes 东/東 only as the traditional character 東's cursive-derived simplified form; 东 itself is not analyzed as containing independent 日 and 木 semantic components. This supports no component-origin claim for modern 东 beyond graphic derivation.
evidence.title: Explaining the Directions 東西南北, part 1: 東西

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: historical script forms and competing interpretations
evidence.text: The database page presents oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and manuscript form categories and a graph-history discussion. The visible text reports an early sack interpretation and a later Shuowen 日/木 interpretation. Forms evolve into later 東, but the exact stepwise graphical transformations were not individually inspected as glyph images in this research; the visual sources are image links. No image inspection is claimed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：東字檢索

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The database says 甲金文 束 depicts binding both ends of a sack and that oracle-bone 束 can also be read for 東/east. This offers graphic and borrowing context for related graph forms, but does not independently recover the sack's name or prove the relevant lexical sound match.

search_audit.outcome: Outlier and Wiktionary identify reconstructed east 東 and related 束/橐 comparisons; Baxter-Sagart book PDF confirms fanqie methodology, but does not provide independent reconstruction of the depicted sack's name. gaps: The proposed bag/sack graphic origin is supported by the CUHK database and Outlier but disputed in a peer-reviewed NCKU article; not all early 東 occurrences are demonstrably used with a bag sense.

The whole-graph sound-loan hypothesis requires a source lexeme for the depicted object. The sources do not independently establish the object's ancient name or pronunciation; reconstructing 東 alone cannot establish that source name. The specific loan sound match therefore remains unverified.
Oracle-bone example 合集9735「東土受年」 is reported in the inspected CUHK database, but the inscription itself was not independently inspected here.
Shijing 小星 provides a directional literary attestation, but its exact composition date and earliest physical witness were not established in the inspected page.
No exact date for when host/landlord senses first emerged was found; the seating explanation is reported, while its earliest attestation is not established.
The semantic bridges to listed spring and toilet senses are not established; they are dictionary glosses only and have not been arranged into a chronology.

Modern simplified 东 is directly described by Outlier as cursive-derived, but no individual early cursive specimen was visually inspected; the exact dated graphic path to standardized simplified 东 remains incompletely documented in this research.

No proposed semantic or phonetic components in modern 东 can be classified as inherited 日 or 木 components: the graph is treated as a cursive-derived whole form. For 東, the database describes the early object graph rather than semantic 日/木 constituents; the 日+木 analysis is attributed to Shuowen's historical account.
